title: Frame (JSON serialization)
description: Schema for a Frame written in the JSON serialization: a single object whose members are the metadata fields, with the body carried as the 'body' string. This is the same Frame shape the frontmatter schema describes, with the body included as data. Extension fields are permitted.

type.$comment: Required. The self-identifying hook. Exactly 'frame', or 'frame [<major>.<minor>]'. The bracketed token names the spec conformance family; patch-qualified tokens such as 'frame [0.2.0]' are not valid. Note that the JSON serialization is defined by the working draft targeting v0.3, so a JSON Frame that declares a version should declare 'frame [0.3]' or later.

name.$comment: Required. Short human-readable name for the Frame.

description.$comment: Required. One or two sentences on what the Frame is for and when it should be used.

visibility.$comment: Required. Not a closed set: the spec suggests these four values but does not restrict the field to them, so this is 'examples' rather than 'enum'.

version.$comment: Recommended. The Frame's own revision, not the spec version. The spec does not mandate a versioning scheme, so no pattern is enforced.

scope.$comment: Recommended. Where the Frame applies. The spec defines no formal scope grammar.

maintainer.$comment: Recommended. Person, team, or organization that maintains the Frame.

inherits.$comment: Recommended. One parent Frame as a string, or several as an array. Earlier entries have lower precedence than later ones; the child always wins. Values are references an implementation can resolve, typically a path, name, or URI. Parents may be written in a different serialization.

body.$comment: Optional, and the part that carries the value. Free-form human-readable text, conventionally Markdown. The spec defines no required sections and no section taxonomy, so nothing about its content is constrained here. An empty or absent body validates and conveys nothing.
